source.author: verg
source.text: Aeneas neque enim patrius consistere mentem passus amor rapidum ad navis praemittit Achaten, Ascanio ferat haec, ipsumque ad moenia ducat; omnis in Ascanio cari stat cura parentis.
source.text_original: Aeneas (neque enim patrius consistere mentem / passus amor) rapidum ad navis praemittit Achaten, / Ascanio ferat haec, ipsumque ad moenia ducat; / omnis in Ascanio cari stat cura parentis.
source.text_english: Aeneas, for his native love did not allow his mind to settle, sends swift Achates ahead to the ships, to bring these things to Ascanius and to lead him himself to the walls; all the care of a loving father rests upon Ascanius.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: quin ego, nequa metu nimio me cura parentis impediat, fallam ignarum subitusque paratis tunc adero, primas linquet cum puppis harenas.
reuse.text_original: quin ego, nequa metu nimio me cura parentis / impediat, fallam ignarum subitusque paratis / tunc adero, primas linquet cum puppis harenas.
reuse.text_english: Rather, lest any concern for my father hinder me with excessive fear, I shall deceive him, unaware as he is, and suddenly I shall be present, with my preparations made, when the ship leaves the first sands.
